newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slips but U.S. arbitrage bolsters bull.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slips but U.S. arbitrage bolsters bull.

text.p: NWE naphtha fell slightly on Thursday but traders said the sharp propane rally in the U.S. was keeping the arbitrage open or at least close to open, reinforcing expectations for near-term strength.

"Three cargoes were definitely done for about 95,000 tonnes and the question is whether another one was done today," one source said, who said there were rumors that a 25,000 tonne cargo was looking to shipped to the U.S.
He said the colder weather in the U.S. was pushing up propane prices and as a result petchem demand was rising for naphtha from NWE, particularly for full range materials.
U.S. spot propane continued to climb on Thursday after inventory data showed a drop of 1.4 million barrels and forecasts called for cold weather in most of the U.S.
Dec swaps slipped $2.50 to $221.50/$222.50 with Jan $6 behind at $214.50/$215.50. Feb swaps fell $3.50 to $208/$209.
Cargoes were notionally put at $225/$227 cif, unchanged.

Algeria's Skikda port remained closed on Thursday to most maritime traffic because of bad weather but should open again by midday on Friday, a port official said.Traders said the closure since Tuesday had not affected prices.
